coachMessages.text: The overcut: when both threats are on the same parity row, the upper threat wins — it reaches the win first.

slides.infoProse: Red has a three-in-a-row at row 0 (columns 0–2, lower threat) and Yellow at row 2 (columns 0–2, upper threat). Both are even parity rows. Because they share parity, the lower threat does not kill the upper — Yellow's upper threat prevails.

coachMessages.text: Yellow's upper threat neutralizes Red's lower threat by reaching the winning cell first. Parity advantage flips the column.

slides.infoProse: With an extra Red disc at column 6 to show a more developed game, the overcut remains strong. The same-parity rule means Yellow's upper threat at row 2 wins regardless of the lower threat at row 0.
